title: Adaptive rollback playbook and state reconciliation for batching/cache config changes
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Background: Recent automated tuning runs adjusted batching and prefix/KV cache parameters to reduce per-token cost for latency-tolerant tenants. Some customers and internal benchmarks saw transient throughput improvements but a subset experienced increased tail latency and cache-miss amplification during cold starts. This ticket designs and implements an adaptive automatic rollback system specifically for batching and cache-related config changes that: (1) defines expressive triggers tied to cost/latency/quality signals, (2) enforces guarded apply workflows (preflight -> shadow -> staged canary -> promote), and (3) performs deterministic state reconciliation for KV/prefix caches and warmup steps during rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Define and document a minimum set of triggers (cost spike, 95p latency regressed >15%, token error-rate >1%) that will automatically schedule a rollback and emit a runbook event.
A2: Implement a guarded-apply pipeline that supports dry-run (simulate), shadow-apply (mirror traffic), and staged canary rollout with automated rollback at configurable thresholds.
A3: Rollback operation must be idempotent and perform cache state reconciliation: restore snapshot or trigger deterministic cache warmup for 90% of affected prefixes within 10 minutes.
A4: Provide observability: per-change timeline in Console UI, including detected trigger, decision path, affected nodes, and a causal diff of batching/cache params.
A5: End-to-end tests (unit+integration) simulating injected faults validate that rollback triggers fire and state reaches expected baseline within SLOs.
A6: Include a non-disruptive manual override and an audit log entry for every automatic rollback event.
A7: No P0 customer incidents attributable to this feature during an opt-in beta across 2 weeks of production traffic for three pilot customers.
A8: Documentation (runbook + Confluence) completed and reviewed by Reliability and Product teams.
A9: Security review completed for any snapshot/restore mechanics involving persisted cache state (KMS/HSM integration if needed).
technical_design: Core idea: treat batching/cache parameter change as a stateful, multi-step transaction. The pipeline will be implemented as: 1) Preflight: local simulation using representative traffic traces (from runtime-lite harness). 2) Shadow apply: push parameters to a shadow pool routed from a small percentage of real requests (1-2%) and compare outputs/timings without affecting real responses. 3) Canary ramp: staged rollout across pods (5% -> 25% -> 50%) with automated gate checks. 4) Promote: full rollout. 5) Automated rollback: if any gate fails, run the rollback actor which re-applies previous config and executes a state reconciliation subroutine. State reconciliation: - if snapshot available within retention window, restore KV/prefix snapshot for affected model shard(s) (uses S3 with KMS encryption); - otherwise run deterministic cold-warm procedure that replays recent requests into cache in background while respecting latency SLOs (throttled warmup); - annotate affected shards and mark for manual follow-up if warmup doesn't meet threshold. Safety guardrails: pre-apply cost/latency simulations, per-tenant limits to avoid broad blast radius, circuit-breaker to pause automated rollouts when cluster-level anomalies detected. Implementation notes: introduce a idempotent change token tied to config version, persist change metadata to change-store (append-only) and ensure reconcile step reads change token to validate expected state before modifications. Provide a small state machine library (apply -> observe -> rollback -> reconcile -> close) that is pluggable for other config types beyond batching/cache.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal feature flag behind 'adaptive_rollback' - enable on staging clusters. Run synthetic stability matrix for 48h.
Phase 1: Canary with low-traffic internal tenants (2 tenants) for 72h. Monitor metrics and runbook activation rate.
Phase 2: Opt-in beta with 3 pilot customers (billing/infra teams) for 2 weeks with console visibility and daily syncs.
Phase 3: Gradual enablement across Controlled hosts (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with escalation path to on-call and exec notifications.
Phase 4: Full rollout and deprecation of legacy manual rollback scripts.
Safety windows: allow manual pause and forced-rollback button in Console for the on-call during any phase.

Rollback behavior: automatic rollback executes with a soft-threshold first (attempt reconciliation + warmup), if reconciliation time exceeds configured timeout or metrics still degraded then execute hard revert and notify customers and stakeholders.
test_plan: Unit tests for change-state state machine and idempotency semantics.
Integration tests in runtime-lite that simulate cache-miss storms and validate warmup strategy meets 90% prefix hit target within allotted time.
Chaos test: inject node failures mid-canary to validate rollback remains consistent and does not orphan change tokens.
E2E in staging with 3 representative model families and traffic mixes to ensure cost improvements without tail-latency regressions.
Safety regression suite to run on every change to the adaptive-rollback service (CI gate).
metrics: Primary: delta in per-token cost for affected tenants (before/after, 24h rolling)
Primary: 95th and 99th percentile latencies during and after rollout
SLOs: rollback-to-stable time (target median < 5 minutes; P95 < 15 minutes)
Cache metrics: prefix hit-rate recovery curve and time-to-90% recovery
Operational: number of automatic rollbacks per 1000 changes (target < 2%), average severity of rollbacks
Customer impact: number of customer-facing incidents attributable to automated rollbacks
